title: A call for evidence‐based conservation: Securing the future of waterbirds along the East Asian‐Australasian flyway
content:
The modified PSR framework proved valuable for assessing conservation effectiveness and identifying research gaps for waterbirds in the EAAF. Recognizing similar threats to other migratory species globally, we urge action to: (1) prioritize regionally relevant research validating frontline conservation actions, (2) enhance communication between researchers and practitioners and (3) expand evidence databases with relevant spatial and taxonomic representation. Implementing these steps will strengthen the evidence base, better align research with on-the-ground needs and improve the long-term prospects for migratory species in Asia.


Abstract

Migratory species worldwide face escalating anthropogenic pressures, yet effective conservation requires transboundary strategies across their ranges. This is particularly evident in the East Asian-Australasian Flyway (EAAF), a region vital for migratory waterbirds and home to a third of the global human population. Despite its ecological importance and the numerous threats impacting waterbird populations, a systematic, evidence-based assessment of conservation actions is lacking. We investigated the conservation actions implemented by reserve managers in the EAAF, focusing on their perceived threats and associated management strategies. We then compared these practitioner-driven priorities with the scientific evidence available in the conservation evidence (CE), using a modified pressure–state–response (PSR) framework to structure the linkage between implemented actions and evidence. This comparison allowed us to identify potential gaps between conservation practice and scientific knowledge, highlighting key research areas for improved, evidence-based species conservation along the flyway. Our results revealed discrepancies between perceived threats and the evidence in the CE to support management actions. Habitat loss and human disturbance were prioritized by the reserve managers, but evidence for the effectiveness of some management practices was limited. Biological invasions were a lower priority for managers, despite there is a comparable evidence base for justifying the action. This indicates a mismatch between research focus and on-the-ground needs. Furthermore, the existing CE database has limited evidence specific to the EAAF. Synthesis and application: The modified PSR framework proved valuable for assessing conservation effectiveness and identifying research gaps for waterbirds in the EAAF. Recognizing similar threats to other migratory species globally, we urge action to: (1) prioritize regionally relevant research validating frontline conservation actions, (2) enhance communication between researchers and practitioners and (3) expand evidence databases with relevant spatial and taxonomic representation. Implementing these steps will strengthen the evidence base, better align research with on-the-ground needs and improve the long-term prospects for migratory species in Asia.

摘要

全球的遷徙物種正面臨日益加劇的人為壓力。因此，保育工作需涵蓋其整體棲息範圍，並實踐跨國的協同保育。這一點在「東亞—澳大利西亞遷飛路線」(East Asian–Australasian Flyway, 下稱EAAF)中尤為明顯。該地區對遷徙水鳥至關重要，同時亦居住著全球三分之一的人口。儘管此區域具有高度生態重要性，但在多重威脅影響水鳥族群的情況下，迄今仍缺乏一套系統化、以證據為本的保育行動評估。 本研究探討了 EAAF 內保護區管理者所執行的保育行動，旨在分析他們所認為的環境威脅及相應的管理策略。接著，我們利用修訂的「壓力–狀態–回應」(Pressure-State-Response, 下稱PSR)模型，比對實際保育行動與(Conservation Evidence, 下稱CE)資料庫中的科學證據。透過分析兩者間的差異，我們指出未來需強化研究的領域，以促進在EAAF內以證據為本的遷飛路線保育。 我們的結果顯示，管理者對威脅的看法與 CE 中支持其保育行動的證據之間存在差異。問卷結果顯示，保護區管理者優先關注棲地喪失與人為干擾；然而，部分現行保育及棲地管理措施，仍缺乏充足的科學證據支持其有效性。相對地，生物入侵對管理者而言仍屬次要議題，儘管相關防治行動已有相當的證據與評估支持。這反映出科學界研究焦點與現實需求之間的落差。此外，現有的 CE 資料庫針對 EAAF 的特定證據及評估仍然相對有限。 綜合與應用:修訂的 PSR 模型在評估 EAAF 水鳥保育成效與辨存研究缺口方面展現了價值。鑑於全球除了水鳥以外也有其他遷徙物種面臨類似威脅，我們建議採取下列行動:(1)優先推動與區域相關的研究，以驗證前線保育行動的成效；(2)強化研究人員與實務工作者之間的溝通；以及(3)擴充證據資料庫，使其涵蓋更廣泛的地理區域與物種類群。落實上述措施將有助於強化保育證據基礎，使研究方向更貼近實務需求，並長遠改善亞洲遷徙物種的生存前景。
